title: The Suez and Panama Canals
body:
The Suez and the Panama Canals are two vital man-made navigation canals that serve as gateways of commerce for both the eastern and western worlds. The Suez Canal was constructed in 1869 in Egypt between Port Said in the north and Port Suez in the south, linking the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea. It gives Europe a new gateway to the Indian Ocean and reduces the sea distance between Liverpool and Colombo compared to the Cape of Good Hope route. It is a sea-level canal without locks, about 160 km long and 11 to 15 m deep. About 100 ships travel through it daily, each taking 10-12 hours to cross. The tolls are so heavy that some ships find it cheaper to go by the longer Cape route whenever the delay is not important.

The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic Ocean in the east to the Pacific Ocean in the west. It was constructed across the Panama Isthmus between Panama City and Colon by the U.S. government. The canal is about 72 km long and has a six-lock system through which ships cross different levels (26 m up and down) before entering the Gulf of Panama. It shortens the sea distance between New York and San Francisco by 13,000 km. Its economic significance is relatively less than that of the Suez, but it is vital to the economies of Latin America.
